story: The University of Texas at Arlington published an account on September 10th, 2026 of an AI conversational tutor built on a National Science Foundation grant, designed so that it will not provide answers and instead prompts the student with questions until the student reaches the answer. The same release says the researcher has already begun testing the system with the Fort Worth Police Department on de-escalation training, and a footnote records that the police work is sponsored by the department and funded by the United States Department of Justice under a separate grant. The federal award record for the tutor gives a start date of October 1st, 2026, which is after the date the university published the account.

claims.quote: UTA develops AI tutor that teaches, not tells
claims.source_title: The University of Texas at Arlington, UTA develops AI tutor that teaches, not tells
claims.notes: Snapshot out/2026-09-16/sources/uta-ai-tutor-2026-09-10.txt. Re-fetched live this run at 200. UTA is a state university, which is why this is filed primary_official rather than primary_corporate, and it is still the institution's own account of its own project.

rejected.finding: That the university's $750,000 and the federal record's 749999 are the same number, or that one is a rounding of the other.
rejected.reason: They are two different strings printed by two different bodies and this run does not reconcile them. No arithmetic was performed on any of the three printed forms and none may be. A deck that wants one figure cites one source and says which.

rejected.finding: That the National Science Foundation grant pays for the Fort Worth Police Department training.
rejected.reason: FLATLY REFUTED BY THE RELEASE'S OWN FOOTNOTE at c19. Two funders, two agencies, two grant numbers. Any copy implying a single federal grant behind both uses is wrong on the source's own words.

rejected.finding: A Fort Worth Police Department primary document about the de-escalation training.
rejected.reason: NOT FETCHED AND NOT FORCED. fortworthtexas.gov serves a robots.txt naming no AI agent but carrying roughly 1,500 Disallow directives whose full list could not be enumerated reliably. Fetching a path without knowing whether it sits inside that list would be guessing at a crawl boundary, which this project does not do.

rejected.finding: A Department of Justice award record for Grant No. 15PBJA-23-GG-06172-NTCP.
rejected.reason: REACHED FOR AND ABSENT. ojp.gov/robots.txt permits the funding path and names no AI agent, and the canonical award url returned HTTP 404 with no body. The grant number is carried only as a string the university printed.

rejected.finding: Normalising the apostrophes in the release's quotes, or asserting they are curly.
rejected.reason: UNSETTLED ON ONE CHARACTER CLASS. Quotes were chosen to begin after the apostrophe wherever the fact survived the trim. Where it could not, at c8, the full string is carried at medium confidence. NO SLIDE MAY SILENTLY CHANGE THIS CHARACTER IN A QUOTATION.

rejected.finding: That Shuchi Deb and Shuchisnigdha Deb should be printed as one name, or that either source has the name wrong.
rejected.reason: Two printed forms of one person's name on two sources, carried as such at c5 and c28. Neither was corrected against the other.

rejected.finding: A count of the researchers on the project taken from the release.
rejected.reason: The release names two people and then says along with several of Deb's department colleagues. Several is not a count. The federal record's array has four entries and that count is carried at c29 from the federal record alone.

rejected.finding: Any course name, course number or course title for the tutor deployment.
rejected.reason: NEITHER SOURCE GIVES ONE. The count and the discipline are carried at c33 and that is the whole of what either source supports.

rejected.finding: Tarrant County as a fact stated by either source.
rejected.reason: The word Tarrant appears on neither source. The ledger's Tarrant County scoping is the record's own geography and is recorded as an absence at a2, not as a sourced claim.

rejected.finding: Any evaluation result, accuracy figure, number of officers trained or number of students taught.
rejected.reason: NEITHER SOURCE PUBLISHES ONE. Recorded as an absence at a3. A deck may not say the tutor works or that the police training improved anything.

rejected.finding: That the six levels of Bloom's Revised Taxonomy in the published literature should correct the abstract's five levels.
rejected.reason: The abstract's own numeral is carried at c34. Supplying a sixth level would be this run producing a numeral no source printed.

rejected.finding: That the federal start date of 10/01/2026 contradicts the release's statement that police testing has already begun.
rejected.reason: Not a contradiction. The police work is funded by a separate Department of Justice grant per c19, so it is not governed by the NSF award's start date at all.

rejected.finding: Reproducing the four co-principal investigators' email addresses on any published surface.
rejected.reason: The addresses sit inside the federal record's coPDPI field. The quotes at c29 are trimmed to the names for that reason. Published copy names the four people and stops.

absences.assertion: Neither source names a single course by title or by number. The federal abstract gives a count and a discipline and the university release gives neither.
absences.document: UTA release of September 10th, 2026, and NSF Award Search record for award 2539663
absences.how_it_was_looked_for: Every occurrence of the word course in the release was examined. There are two and neither attaches a title, a number or a level. The federal abstractText was then read in full and its only course reference gives a count, a discipline and a year range and no identifier.
absences.what_it_does_not_prove: It is not evidence that the courses are undecided. The honest form is that neither published source identifies them.

absences.assertion: Neither source names a county. The record item's Tarrant County scoping comes from nowhere in either document.
absences.document: UTA release of September 10th, 2026, and NSF Award Search record for award 2539663
absences.how_it_was_looked_for: The release was searched for the word Tarrant and returned none. The complete set of place names on it is Arlington, Fort Worth, Dallas-Fort Worth and North Texas. The federal record was read field by field for a geographic key and carries city, state, district and zip, and no county field at all.
absences.what_it_does_not_prove: It does not mean the work is not in Tarrant County. Arlington and Fort Worth both sit in it. The honest form is that the county is the record's own geography rather than a fact either source states.

absences.assertion: Neither source publishes any evaluation result for the tutor or for the police training. Every statement about what the system does is design intent or future tense.
absences.document: UTA release of September 10th, 2026, and NSF Award Search record for award 2539663
absences.how_it_was_looked_for: Every sentence of the release describing the system was read and its verb examined. Nine are future tense and three are present tense, and none of the three reports an outcome. The federal abstract's evaluation language is future tense on an award whose start date is 10/01/2026.
absences.what_it_does_not_prove: It is not evidence that the system does not work, and it is not evidence that no internal result exists. The award had not started on the date of this run according to its own record.

absences.assertion: No primary document from the Fort Worth Police Department, the City of Fort Worth or the Department of Justice about this training was obtained this run. The Department of Justice grant number rests on the university's footnote alone.
absences.document: City of Fort Worth robots.txt, Office of Justice Programs robots.txt, and the OJP funding award page
absences.how_it_was_looked_for: fortworthtexas.gov/robots.txt was fetched first and carries roughly 1,500 Disallow directives that could not be enumerated reliably, so no path on that host was fetched. ojp.gov/robots.txt permits the funding path, and the award page at the canonical path returned HTTP 404 with no body.
absences.what_it_does_not_prove: It is not evidence that the grant does not exist or that the training is not happening. A 404 on one canonical path says nothing about whether the award is recorded elsewhere. The honest form is that the university states the grant number and this run could not corroborate it from a federal source.
